hints.title: Nested Substring Reversal Overhead Obstacle
hints.text: Reversing substrings repeatedly inside-out incurs quadratic runtime for deeply nested parentheses. How can precomputing matching bracket pairs allow walking through the string with alternating directions in linear time?

hints.title: Wormhole Teleportation Invariant
hints.text: Whenever traversal hits a parenthesis, it teleports to its matching partner and inverts its step direction. Every character is traversed exactly once in the final printed order.

hints.title: Pairing and Direction Alternation Procedure
hints.text: Find matching index pairs for all parentheses using an index buffer. Then traverse starting at index 0 with step = 1: if s[i] is '(' or ')', jump to pair[i] and negate step; otherwise append s[i] to the result. Advance by step until out of bounds.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of string s (1 <= N <= 2000)
complexity.notes: Two-phase linear time solution using wormhole teleportation between matching parentheses.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Repeatedly finding innermost parentheses and inverting substrings takes O(N^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Storing matched index pairings in an O(N) array eliminates string copies and guarantees strict O(N) runtime.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Discovering or explaining the O(N) wormhole traversal algorithm rather than accepting the naive O(N^2) solution.
